# BAD-041 — Split renderer/app.js (8991 lines) into renderer/app/ classic scripts

## Brief
Plan: [[docs/spikes/bad-036/renderer-app|renderer-app spike]] (Estima, BADS-036). Measured at 20d11e1: 471 top-level bindings in one classic script, zero load-time forward references.

Proposed: 43 contiguous classic scripts under renderer/app/, loaded by tag in today's order between reel.js and a ~110-line app.js. app.js keeps its path and tag and takes the boot block, both long-lived timers and every window.vc push subscription, so a push from main cannot land between two tags on an unloaded part. Ten files over 250 are argued (table read 377, reel 339, library rail 329, collab actions 328, collab home rows 321, and five between 253 and 268), with optional cuts and optional merges listed for Eric. No CSP or build.files change. test/audiorate.test.js and test/fonts.test.js pin app.js text and move with the code.

Cross-ticket: the --smoke walkthrough's renderer-name list in the main.js spike, section 2e, is part of this file's contract; the main.js split must not rename those names either.

Verification: the concatenation check (parts in tag order minus their two-line headers diff against the original as pure moves), npm test, and a full npm run smoke with BT_LIBRARY_ROOT at a copy of fixtures/library. Settings, updates, collab and the export dialogs are invisible to smoke and are proven by the concatenation check plus the manual opens in section 8.

**Gate.** Queued until Eric approves the proposed file layout in the spike. Phase 2 does not start before that approval, and an approval that changes the layout is written into the spike's section 4 first.

**Rules for Phase 2, from BAD-036.** Split by responsibility; 250 lines is where a file gets a second look, not a cap, and every file left over 250 is argued in the spike's section 6. Every PR is a pure move: no statement is edited, a bug found on the way is its own ticket, and the spike's behaviour-preservation check (section 8) runs on every PR. The public surface in section 2 is the compatibility contract and does not change. Extraction order follows section 9: shared constants, types and pure utilities first, then state and services, then sub-components or handlers, then the entry file reduced to an orchestrator. Verification is the implementing-changes skill's tier for the files touched, quoted in each PR.

## Size, persona and model decision
Phase 2: one engineer on opus per PR in the spike's section 9, in a worktree on a feat/bad-nnn branch after bash scripts/worktree-init.sh; a reviewer at fable tier (opus while the Fable limit holds) checks each PR's pure-move proof before it lands.
